397311.title: Ieum — Expansion: K-Museum Regional Touring Exhibition
397311.overview: A touring exhibition from the K-Museum programme, which sends collections out from national institutions to regional museums. It is hosted here by the Daegu Textile Museum — Daegu was the centre of Korea's textile industry through the twentieth century, and the museum covers that history alongside the fabric itself. Free.

397205.title: Variations on Contemporary Colour Field Abstraction: Dieter Balzer and Im So-a
397205.overview: A two-person show pairing the Austrian artist Dieter Balzer with the Korean painter Im So-a, both working in colour field abstraction — flat planes of colour rather than gesture or image. Balzer's work extends off the canvas into geometric wall installations. Free, in a commercial gallery in central Daegu.

397407.title: Variations on Contemporary Colour Field Abstraction: Dieter Balzer and Im So-a
397407.overview: A two-person show pairing the Austrian artist Dieter Balzer with the Korean painter Im So-a, both working in colour field abstraction — flat planes of colour rather than gesture or image. Open 10:00–18:00 on weekdays and 11:00–17:00 on Saturdays; closed Sundays and public holidays. Booking a day ahead is recommended. Free.

397466.title: The State of Things That Cannot Be Explained
397466.overview: A project exhibition by artists working on site in Jeonju, held at Gyodong Art Center — a contemporary art space inside Jeonju Hanok Village, a few minutes from Gyeonggijeon Shrine. Free, and easy to fold into a walk around the hanok village.

397408.title: Trace: A Conversation of Surfaces
397408.overview: A two-person show by Yu Hui and the German sculptor Dietrich Klinge, running 9–30 September. Neither artist erases the marks their tools leave: Yu pushes paint across the surface with a squeegee, Klinge cuts into wood with saw and chisel. What remains in the pushed and carved areas is the movement of the body and the time caught in it. Held in a converted cinema in Gohan, a former coal-mining town in the Gangwon mountains. Free.

397495.title: Words That Prop the Door: Haeum Saedeul Open Studio #4
397495.venue: Haeum Saedeul Art Creation Space, Ilsan Lake Park
397495.overview: An open-studio day at Goyang's artist residency inside Ilsan Lake Park, where resident artists open their working spaces and show what they have been making. Free, and a chance to see work in progress rather than a finished exhibition. Ilsan Lake Park is one of the largest artificial lake parks in Asia and worth the visit on its own.

396965.title: Jo Hui-yeong Gayageum Recital: Melodies of Light II
396965.overview: A solo recital on the gayageum, the twelve-stringed Korean zither, in a small hall built specifically for traditional music — timber-framed and acoustically live, so the instrument is heard unamplified. The theatre sits directly opposite Donhwamun, the main gate of Changdeokgung Palace. Free admission, which for a full solo recital in central Seoul is unusual.

397433.title: The Angle of the Heart: Views That Dissolve Boundaries
397433.overview: A group exhibition at Maru Art Center in Insadong, Seoul's traditional crafts and gallery quarter. Free, and a short walk from Jogyesa Temple and Gyeongbokgung.

397462.title: Surim New Wave 2026: Kim Hyo-yeong — A Sidelong Gaze
397462.price: 30,000 won, all seats (50% off for artists, repeat attendees and Dongdaemun-gu residents)
397462.overview: Part of Surim New Wave, a series that commissions younger Korean traditional musicians to make new work rather than perform the repertoire. Kim Hyo-yeong plays the geomungo, the six-stringed zither struck with a bamboo stick — the deepest-voiced of the Korean string instruments and historically the scholar's instrument.

397463.title: Surim New Wave 2026: Lee Hwa-yeong — Hwaryeong, You Shall Be at Ease
397463.price: 30,000 won, all seats (50% off for artists and repeat attendees)
397463.overview: Part of Surim New Wave, a series commissioning new work from younger Korean traditional musicians. The title takes its Chinese characters from a phrase meaning to be brought to ease, and the programme builds a contemporary set around that idea.

397464.title: Surim New Wave 2026: Lee Na-yeon — Gwiryu, Returning Current
397464.price: 30,000 won, all seats (50% off for artists, repeat attendees and Dongdaemun-gu residents)
397464.overview: The third in the Surim New Wave 2026 series of commissioned work by younger Korean traditional musicians, closing the season in early November.
